directives.name: accelerator
directives.description:
The `accelerator` directive allows you to request hardware accelerators (e.g. GPUs) for the task execution.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#accelerator)

directives.name: afterScript
directives.description:
The `afterScript` directive allows you to execute a custom (Bash) snippet *after* the task script.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#afterscript)

directives.name: arch
directives.description:
The `arch` directive allows you to define the CPU architecture to build the software used by the task.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#arch)

directives.name: array
directives.description:
The `array` directive allows you to submit tasks as *job arrays* for executors that support it.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#array)

directives.name: beforeScript
directives.description:
The `beforeScript` directive allows you to execute a custom (Bash) snippet *before* the task script.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#beforescript)

directives.name: cache
directives.description:
The `cache` directive allows you to store the process results to a local cache. When the cache is enabled *and* the pipeline is launched with the `-resume` option, any task executions that are already cached will be reused.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#cache)

directives.name: clusterOptions
directives.description:
The `clusterOptions` directive allows the usage of any native configuration option accepted by your cluster submit command. You can use it to request non-standard resources or use settings that are specific to your cluster and not supported out of the box by Nextflow.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#clusteroptions)

directives.name: conda
directives.description:
The `conda` directive allows for the definition of the process dependencies using the [Conda](https://conda.io) package manager.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#conda)

directives.name: container
directives.description:
The `container` directive allows you to execute the process script in a container.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#container)

directives.name: containerOptions
directives.description:
The `containerOptions` directive allows you to specify any container execution option supported by the underlying container engine (ie. Docker, Singularity, etc). This can be useful to provide container settings only for a specific process.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#containeroptions)

directives.name: cpus
directives.description:
The `cpus` directive allows you to define the number of (logical) CPUs required by each task.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#cpus)

directives.name: debug
directives.description:
The `debug` directive allows you to print the process standard output to Nextflow's standard output, i.e. the console. By default this directive is disabled.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#debug)

directives.name: disk
directives.description:
The `disk` directive allows you to define how much local disk storage the process is allowed to use.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#disk)

directives.name: errorStrategy
directives.description:
The `errorStrategy` directive allows you to define what to do when a task fails.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#errorstrategy)

directives.name: executor
directives.description:
The `executor` defines the underlying system where tasks are executed.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#executor)

directives.name: ext
directives.description:
The `ext` is a special directive used for custom settings by some executors.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#ext)

directives.name: fair
directives.description:
The `fair` directive, when enabled, guarantees that process outputs will be emitted in the order in which they were received.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#fair)

directives.name: hints
directives.description:
The `hints` directive specifies executor-specific hints as key-value pairs. Keys may be namespaced with an `executor/` prefix to target a specific executor.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#hints)

directives.name: label
directives.description:
The `label` directive allows you to annotate a process with a mnemonic identifier of your choice.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#label)

directives.name: machineType
directives.description:
The `machineType` directive can be used to specify a predefined Google Compute Platform [machine type](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/machine-types) when using the [Google Batch](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/executor/google-batch) executor.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#machinetype)

directives.name: maxErrors
directives.description:
The `maxErrors` directive allows you to specify the maximum number of times a process can fail when using the `retry` or `ignore` error strategy. By default this directive is disabled.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#maxerrors)

directives.name: maxForks
directives.description:
The `maxForks` directive allows you to define the maximum number of tasks (per process) that can be executed in parallel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#maxforks)

directives.name: maxRetries
directives.description:
The `maxRetries` directive allows you to define the maximum number of times a task can be retried when using the `retry` error strategy. By default only one retry is allowed.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#maxretries)

directives.name: maxSubmitAwait
directives.description:
The `maxSubmitAwait` directives allows you to specify how long a task can remain in the submission queue. If a task remains in the queue beyond this time limit, it will fail.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#maxsubmitawait)

directives.name: memory
directives.description:
The `memory` directive allows you to define how much memory is required by each task. Can be a string (e.g. `'8 GB'`) or a memory unit (e.g. `8.GB`).

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#memory)

directives.name: module
directives.description:
The `module` directive allows you to provide software dependencies to a process using [Environment Modules](http://modules.sourceforge.net/).

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#module)

directives.name: penv
directives.description:
The `penv` directive allows you to define the parallel environment to be used when submitting a parallel task to the [SGE](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/executor/sge) resource manager.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#penv)

directives.name: pod
directives.description:
The `pod` directive allows you to define pod specific settings, such as environment variables, secrets, and config maps, when using the [Kubernetes](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/executor/kubernetes) executor.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#pod)

directives.name: publishDir
directives.description:
The `publishDir` directive allows you to publish the process output files to a directory.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#publishdir)

directives.name: queue
directives.description:
The `queue` directive allows you to specify the queue to which jobs are submitted when using a grid executor.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#queue)

directives.name: resourceLabels
directives.description:
The `resourceLabels` directive allows you to specify custom name-value pairs which are applied to the compute resources used for the process execution.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#resourcelabels)

directives.name: resourceLimits
directives.description:
The `resourceLimits` directive allows you to specify environment-specific limits for task resource requests.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#resourcelimits)

directives.name: scratch
directives.description:
The `scratch` directive allows you to execute each task in a temporary directory that is local to the compute node.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#scratch)

directives.name: secret
directives.description:
The `secret` directive allows you to securely provide secrets to a process.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/secrets#process-directive)

directives.name: shell
directives.description:
The `shell` directive allows you to define a custom shell command for process scripts. By default, script blocks are executed with `/bin/bash -ue`.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#shell)

directives.name: spack
directives.description:
The `spack` directive allows you to provide software dependencies using the [Spack](https://spack.io) package manager.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#spack)

directives.name: stageInMode
directives.description:
The `stageInMode` directive defines how input files are staged into the task work directory.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#stageinmode)

directives.name: stageOutMode
directives.description:
The `stageOutMode` directive defines how output files are staged out from the scratch directory to the task work directory when using the `scratch` directive.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#stageoutmode)

directives.name: storeDir
directives.description:
The `storeDir` directive allows you to use an external directory as a *permanent* cache for process outputs.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#storedir)

directives.name: tag
directives.description:
The `tag` directive allows you to associate each process execution with a custom label, so that it will be easier to identify in the log file or in a report.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#tag)

directives.name: time
directives.description:
The `time` directive allows you to define how long a task is allowed to run.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/process#time)

inputs.name: env
inputs.description: Declare an environment variable input. The received value should be a string, and it will be exported to the task environment as an environment variable given by `identifier`.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description:
Declare a file input. The received value should be a file or collection of files.

The argument can be an identifier or string. If an identifier, the received value will be made available to the process body as a variable. If a string, the received value will be staged into the task directory under the given alias.

inputs.name: stdin
inputs.description: Declare a `stdin` input. The received value should be a string, and it will be provided as the standard input (i.e. `stdin`) to the task script. It should be declared only once for a process.

inputs.name: tuple
inputs.description:
Declare a tuple input. Each argument should be an input declaration such as `val`, `path`, `env`, or `stdin`.

The received value should be a tuple with the same number of elements as the `tuple` declaration, and each received element should be compatible with the corresponding `tuple` argument. Each tuple element is treated the same way as if it were a standalone input.

inputs.name: val
inputs.description: Declare a variable input. The received value can be any type, and it will be made available to the process body (i.e. `script`, `shell`, `exec`) as a variable with the given name.

outputs.name: env
outputs.description: Declare an environment variable output. It receives the value of the environment variable given by `identifier` from the task environment.

outputs.name: eval
outputs.description: Declare an `eval` output. It receives the standard output of the given command, which is executed in the task environment after the task script.

outputs.name: path
outputs.description: Declare a file output. It receives the output files from the task environment that match the given pattern.

outputs.name: stdout
outputs.description: Declare a `stdout` output. It receives the standard output of the task script.

outputs.name: tuple
outputs.description: Declare a tuple output. Each argument should be an output declaration such as `val`, `path`, `env`, `stdin`, or `eval`. Each tuple element is treated the same way as if it were a standalone output.

outputs.name: val
outputs.description: Declare a value output. The argument can be any value, and it can reference any output variables defined in the process body (i.e. variables declared without the `def` keyword).

typedOutputs.name: env
typedOutputs.description: Get the value of an environment variable from the task environment.

typedOutputs.name: eval
typedOutputs.description: Get the standard output of the given command, which is executed in the task environment after the task script.

typedOutputs.name: stdout
typedOutputs.description: Get the standard output of the task script.

stage.name: env
stage.description: Declare an environment variable in the task environment with the given name and value.

stage.name: stageAs
stage.description: Stage a file into the task directory under the given alias.

stage.name: stdin
stage.description: Stage the given value as the standard input (i.e. `stdin`) to the task script.

agentDirectives.name: goal
agentDirectives.description: The `goal` directive states a high-level objective that steers the agent's multi-turn loop. It is advisory: the model is encouraged to keep working until the goal is met, while `maxIterations` remains the hard cap.

agentDirectives.name: instruction
agentDirectives.description: The `instruction` directive sets the agent system prompt (its role/persona).

agentDirectives.name: label
agentDirectives.description: The `label` directive annotates the agent with a mnemonic identifier, which can be used to apply configuration in the `agent` scope through a `withLabel:` selector. It can be specified more than once.

agentDirectives.name: maxIterations
agentDirectives.description: The `maxIterations` directive caps the LLM tool-calling loop.

agentDirectives.name: model
agentDirectives.description: The `model` directive selects the LLM in `provider/model` form (e.g. `openai/gpt-5-mini`).

agentDirectives.name: skills
agentDirectives.description: The `skills` directive declares the agent skills (SKILL.md folders) the agent may use. Each entry is a local skill name (resolved under the `skills/` directory beside the script) or a remote GitHub reference (`github.com/<org>/<repo>[@rev]`) cloned and cached into that same `skills/` directory.

agentDirectives.name: tools
agentDirectives.description: The `tools` directive declares the tools the agent may invoke, as namespaced references of the form `family[:group]:name`. `nf:module_run` exposes every in-scope module or process, `nf:module_run:<NAME>` a single one and `nf:module_run:<PREFIX>*` those matching; `fs:*` selects the six sandboxed file tools (`read`, `write`, `edit`, `ls`, `grep`, `find`); `shell:bash` a shell inside the runner container (`pi` runner only). An agent declaring no tools gets none, and a reference matching nothing is an error.

operators.name: collect
operators.description:
The `collect` operator collects all values from a source channel into a list and emits it as a single value.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#collect)

operators.name: combine
operators.description:
The `combine` operator emits every pairwise combination of two channels.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#combine)

operators.name: filter
operators.description:
The `filter` operator emits the values from a source channel that satisfy a condition, discarding all other values.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#filter)

operators.name: flatMap
operators.description:
The `flatMap` operator applies a mapping function to each value from a source channel. The mapping function should return a collection, and each element in the collection is emitted separately.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#flatmap)

operators.name: groupBy
operators.description:
The `groupBy` operator collects values from a source channel into groups based on a grouping key. A tuple is emitted for each group containing the grouping key and collection of values.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#groupby)

operators.name: join
operators.description:
The `join` operator emits the relational join of two source channels using a matching key.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#join)

operators.name: map
operators.description:
The `map` operator applies a mapping function to each value from a source channel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#map)

operators.name: mix
operators.description:
The `mix` operator emits the values from two source channels into a single output channel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#mix)

operators.name: reduce
operators.description:
The `reduce` operator applies an accumulator function sequentially to each value from a source channel, and emits the accumulated value.

The accumulator function takes two parameters -- the accumulated value and the *i*-th emitted value -- and it should return the accumulated result, which is passed to the next invocation with the *i+1*-th value. This process is repeated for each value in the source channel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#reduce)

operators.name: subscribe
operators.description:
The `subscribe` operator performs an action for each value in a source channel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#subscribe)

operators.name: unique
operators.description:
The `unique` operator emits the unique values from a source channel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#unique)

operators.name: until
operators.description:
The `until` operator emits each value from a source channel until a stopping condition is satisfied.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#until)

operators.name: view
operators.description:
The `view` operator prints each value from a source channel to standard output.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#view)

operators.name: flatMap
operators.description:
Transforms the dataflow value into a collection with the given closure and emits the resulting values in a dataflow channel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/value#flatmap)

operators.name: map
operators.description:
Transforms the dataflow value into another dataflow value with the given closure.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/value#map)

operators.name: mix
operators.description:
Emits the dataflow value and the values from another channel into a single output channel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/value#mix)

operators.name: subscribe
operators.description:
Invokes the given closure on the dataflow value.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/value#subscribe)

operators.name: view
operators.description:
Transforms the dataflow value using the given closure and print the result to standard output.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/value#view)

factories.name: empty
factories.description:
Create a channel that emits nothing.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-namespaces/channel#empty)

factories.name: fromFilePairs
factories.description:
Create a channel that emits all file pairs matching a glob pattern.

An optional closure can be used to customize the grouping strategy.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-namespaces/channel#fromfilepairs)

factories.name: fromLineage
factories.description:
Create a channel that emits files from the lineage store matching the given key-value params.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-namespaces/channel#fromlineage)

factories.name: fromList
factories.description:
Create a channel that emits each element in a collection.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-namespaces/channel#fromlist)

factories.name: fromPath
factories.description:
Create a channel that emits all paths matching a name or glob pattern.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-namespaces/channel#frompath)

factories.name: interval
factories.description:
Create a channel that emits an incrementing index (starting from zero) at a periodic interval.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-namespaces/channel#interval)

factories.name: of
factories.description:
Create a channel that emits each argument.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-namespaces/channel#of)

factories.name: topic
factories.description:
Create a channel that emits all values in the given topic.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-namespaces/channel#topic)

factories.name: value
factories.description:
Create a dataflow value bound to the given argument.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-namespaces/channel#value)

factories.name: watchPath
factories.description:
Create a channel that watches a glob pattern and emits matching files as they appear.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-namespaces/channel#watchpath)

constants.name: channel
constants.description:
The `channel` namespace contains the built-in channel factories.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-namespaces/channel)

constants.name: log
constants.description:
The `log` namespace contains functions for logging messages to the console.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-namespaces/log)

constants.name: moduleDir
constants.description: The directory where a module script is located (equivalent to `projectDir` if used in the main script).

constants.name: nextflow
constants.description: The `nextflow` namespace contains information about the current Nextflow runtime.

constants.name: workflow
constants.description: The `workflow` namespace contains information about the current workflow run.

functions.name: branchCriteria

functions.name: env

functions.name: error
functions.description: Throw a script runtime error with an optional error message.

functions.name: exit
functions.description: Stop the pipeline execution and return an exit code and optional error message.

functions.name: file

Get a file from a file name or glob pattern.

*NOTE: This function will return a collection if the glob pattern yields zero or multiple files. Use `files()` to get a collection of files.*

functions.name: files
functions.description: Get a collection of files from a file name or glob pattern.

functions.name: groupKey
functions.description: Create a grouping key to use with the [groupTuple](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/operator#grouptuple) operator.

functions.name: multiMapCriteria
functions.description: Create a multi-map criteria to use with the `multiMap` operator.

functions.name: print
functions.description: Print a value to standard output.

functions.name: printf
functions.description: Print a formatted string with the given values to standard output.

functions.name: println
functions.description: Print a value to standard output with a newline.

functions.name: record
functions.description: Create a record from the given named arguments.

functions.name: sleep
functions.description: Sleep for the given number of milliseconds.

functions.name: tuple
functions.description: Create a tuple from the given arguments.

types.name: Channel
types.description:
A channel is an asynchronous sequence of values. It is used to facilitate dataflow logic in a workflow.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel)

members.name: collect
members.description:
The `collect` operator collects all values from a source channel into a list and emits it as a single value.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#collect)

members.name: combine
members.description:
The `combine` operator emits every pairwise combination of two channels.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#combine)

members.name: filter
members.description:
The `filter` operator emits the values from a source channel that satisfy a condition, discarding all other values.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#filter)

members.name: flatMap
members.description:
The `flatMap` operator applies a mapping function to each value from a source channel. The mapping function should return a collection, and each element in the collection is emitted separately.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#flatmap)

members.name: groupBy
members.description:
The `groupBy` operator collects values from a source channel into groups based on a grouping key. A tuple is emitted for each group containing the grouping key and collection of values.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#groupby)

members.name: join
members.description:
The `join` operator emits the relational join of two source channels using a matching key.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#join)

members.name: map
members.description:
The `map` operator applies a mapping function to each value from a source channel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#map)

members.name: mix
members.description:
The `mix` operator emits the values from two source channels into a single output channel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#mix)

members.name: reduce
members.description:
The `reduce` operator applies an accumulator function sequentially to each value from a source channel, and emits the accumulated value.

The accumulator function takes two parameters -- the accumulated value and the *i*-th emitted value -- and it should return the accumulated result, which is passed to the next invocation with the *i+1*-th value. This process is repeated for each value in the source channel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#reduce)

members.name: subscribe
members.description:
The `subscribe` operator performs an action for each value in a source channel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#subscribe)

members.name: unique
members.description:
The `unique` operator emits the unique values from a source channel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#unique)

members.name: until
members.description:
The `until` operator emits each value from a source channel until a stopping condition is satisfied.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#until)

members.name: view
members.description:
The `view` operator prints each value from a source channel to standard output.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/channel#view)

types.name: Value
types.description:
A dataflow value is an asynchronous value. It is used to facilitate dataflow logic in a workflow.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/value)

members.name: combine
members.description:
Combine two dataflow values.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/value#combine)

members.name: flatMap
members.description:
Transforms the dataflow value into a collection with the given closure and emits the resulting values in a dataflow channel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/value#flatmap)

members.name: map
members.description:
Transforms the dataflow value into another dataflow value with the given closure.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/value#map)

members.name: mix
members.description:
Emits the dataflow value and the values from another channel into a single output channel.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/value#mix)

members.name: subscribe
members.description:
Invokes the given closure on the dataflow value.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/value#subscribe)

members.name: view
members.description:
Transforms the dataflow value using the given closure and print the result to standard output.

[Read more](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/stdlib-types/value#view)

types.name: shim.Iterable
types.description:
An iterable is a trait shared by collections that support iteration.

[Read more](https://nextflow.io/docs/latest/reference/stdlib.html#iterable-e)

members.name: any
members.description: Returns `true` if any element in the iterable satisfies the given condition.

members.name: collect
members.description: Returns a new iterable with each element transformed by the given closure.

members.name: collectMany
members.description: Transforms each element in the iterable into a collection with the given closure and concatenates the resulting collections into a list.

members.name: contains
members.description: Returns `true` if the iterable contains the given value.

members.name: containsAll
members.description: Returns `true` if the iterable contains all values in the given iterable.

members.name: each
members.description: Invoke the given closure for each element in the iterable.

members.name: every
members.description: Returns `true` if every element in the iterable satisfies the given condition.

members.name: find
members.description: Returns the first value in the iterable that satisfies the given condition.

members.name: findAll
members.description: Returns the elements in the iterable that satisfy the given condition.

members.name: groupBy
members.description: Collect the elements of an iterable into groups based on a matching key. The closure should return the key for a given element.

members.name: inject
members.description: Apply the given accumulator to each element in the iterable and return the final accumulated value. The closure should accept two parameters, corresponding to the current accumulated value and the current iterable element, and return the next accumulated value. The first element from the iterable is used as the initial accumulated value.

members.name: isEmpty
members.description: Returns `true` if the iterable is empty.

members.name: join
members.description: Concatenates the string representation of each element in the iterable, with the given string as the separator between each element.

members.name: max
members.description: Returns the maximum element in the iterable according to the given closure. The closure should follow the same semantics as the closure parameter of `toSorted()`.

members.name: min
members.description: Returns the minimum element in the iterable according to the given closure. The closure should follow the same semantics as the closure parameter of `toSorted()`.

members.name: size
members.description: Returns the number of elements in the iterable.

members.name: sum
members.description: Returns the sum of the elements in the iterable. The elements should support addition (`+`).

members.name: toList
members.description: Converts the iterable to a list.

members.name: toSet
members.description: Converts the iterable to a set. Duplicate elements are excluded.

members.name: toSorted
members.description: Returns the iterable as a list sorted according to the given closure. The closure should accept one parameter and transform each element into the value that will be used for comparisons.

members.name: toUnique
members.description: Returns a shallow copy of the iterable with duplicate elements excluded. The closure should follow the same semantics as the closure parameter of `toSorted()`.

types.name: shim.List
types.description:
A list is an ordered collection of elements.

[Read more](https://nextflow.io/docs/latest/reference/stdlib.html#list-e)

members.name: collate
members.description: Collates the list into a list of sub-lists of length `size`, stepping through the list `step` elements for each sub-list. If `keepRemainder` is `true`, any remaining elements are included as a partial sub-list, otherwise they are excluded.

members.name: first
members.description: Returns the first element in the list. Raises an error if the list is empty.

members.name: head
members.description: Equivalent to `first()`.

members.name: indexOf
members.description: Returns the index of the first occurrence of the given value in the list, or -1 if the list does not contain the value.

members.name: indices
members.description: Returns the list of integers from 0 to *n - 1*, where *n* is the number of elements in the list.

members.name: init
members.description: Returns a shallow copy of the list with the last element excluded.

members.name: intersect
members.description: Returns the elements of the list that are also in the given iterable, preserving the order and duplicates of the list.

members.name: last
members.description: Returns the last element in the list. Raises an error if the list is empty.

members.name: reverse
members.description: Returns a shallow copy of the list with the elements reversed.

members.name: subList
members.description: Returns the portion of the list between the given `fromIndex` (inclusive) and `toIndex` (exclusive).

members.name: tail
members.description: Returns a shallow copy of the list with the first element excluded.

members.name: take
members.description: Returns the first *n* elements of the list.

members.name: takeWhile
members.description: Returns the longest prefix of the list where each element satisfies the given condition.

members.name: withIndex
members.description: Returns a list of 2-tuples corresponding to the value and index of each element in the list.

types.name: shim.Map
types.description:
A map associates or "maps" keys to values. Each key can map to at most one value -- a map cannot contain duplicate keys.

[Read more](https://nextflow.io/docs/latest/reference/stdlib.html#map-k-v)

members.name: any
members.description: Returns `true` if any key-value pair in the map satisfies the given condition. The closure should accept two parameters corresponding to the key and value of an entry.

members.name: containsKey
members.description: Returns `true` if the map contains a mapping for the given key.

members.name: containsValue
members.description: Returns `true` if the map maps one or more keys to the given value.

members.name: each
members.description: Invoke the given closure for each key-value pair in the map. The closure should accept two parameters corresponding to the key and value of an entry.

members.name: entrySet
members.description: Returns a set of the key-value pairs in the map.

members.name: every
members.description: Returns `true` if every key-value pair in the map satisfies the given condition. The closure should accept two parameters corresponding to the key and value of an entry.

members.name: isEmpty
members.description: Returns `true` if the map is empty.

members.name: keySet
members.description: Returns a set of the keys in the map.

members.name: size
members.description: Returns the number of key-value pairs in the map.

members.name: subMap
members.description: Returns a sub-map containing the given keys.

members.name: values
members.description: Returns a collection of the values in the map.

types.name: shim.Map.Entry
types.description: A map entry is a key-value pair.

members.name: key
members.description: The key of the entry.

members.name: value
members.description: The value of the entry.

types.name: shim.Path
types.description:
A Path is a handle for hierarchical paths such as local files and directories, HTTP/FTP URLs, and object storage paths (e.g. Amazon S3).

[Read more](https://nextflow.io/docs/latest/reference/stdlib.html#path)

members.name: append
members.description: Appends text to a file without replacing existing content.

members.name: baseName
members.description: Gets the file name without its extension, e.g. `/some/path/file.tar.gz` -> `file.tar`.

members.name: copyTo
members.description: Copies a source file or directory to a target file or directory.

members.name: countFasta
members.description: Counts the number of records in a [FASTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FASTA_format) file. See the {ref}`operator-splitfasta` operator for available options.

members.name: countFastq
members.description: Counts the number of records in a [FASTQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FASTQ_format) file. See the {ref}`operator-splitfastq` operator for available options.

members.name: countJson
members.description: Counts the number of records in a JSON file. See the {ref}`operator-splitjson` operator for available options.

members.name: countLines
members.description: Counts the number of lines in a text file. See the {ref}`operator-splittext` operator for available options.

members.name: delete
members.description: Deletes the file or directory at the given path, returning `true` if the operation succeeds, and `false` otherwise.

members.name: deleteDir
members.description: Deletes a directory and all of its contents.

members.name: eachFile
members.description: Iterates through first-level files and directories.

members.name: eachFileRecurse
members.description: Iterates through files and directories depth-first.

members.name: eachLine
members.description: Iterates over the file, applying the specified closure to each line.

members.name: exists
members.description: Returns `true` if the file exists.

members.name: extension
members.description: Gets the file extension, e.g. `/some/path/file.txt` -> `txt`.

members.name: isDirectory
members.description: Returns `true` if the file is a directory.

members.name: isEmpty
members.description: Returns `true` if the file is empty or does not exist.

members.name: isFile
members.description: Returns `true` if it is a regular file (i.e. not a directory).

members.name: isHidden
members.description: Returns `true` if the file is hidden.

members.name: isLink
members.description: Returns `true` if the file is a symbolic link.

members.name: lastModified
members.description: Returns the file last modified timestamp in Unix time (i.e. milliseconds since January 1, 1970).

members.name: listDirectory
members.description: Returns the first-level elements (files and directories) in a directory.

members.name: listFiles
members.description: Returns the first-level elements (files and directories) in a directory.

members.name: mkdir
members.description: Creates a directory at the given path, returning `true` if the directory is created successfully, and `false` otherwise.

members.name: mkdirs
members.description: Creates a directory at the given path, including any nonexistent parent directories.

members.name: mklink
members.description: Creates a *filesystem link* to a given path.

members.name: moveTo
members.description: Moves a source file or directory to a target file or directory. Follows the same semantics as `copyTo()`.

members.name: name
members.description: Gets the file name, e.g. `/some/path/file.txt` -> `file.txt`.

members.name: parent
members.description: Gets the file parent path, e.g. `/some/path/file.txt` -> `/some/path`.

members.name: permissions
members.description: Returns a file's permissions using the [symbolic notation](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File_system_permissions#Symbolic_notation), e.g. `'rw-rw-r--'`.

members.name: readLines
members.description: Reads the file line by line and returns the content as a list of strings.

members.name: relativize
members.description: Returns the relative path between this path and the given path.

members.name: renameTo
members.description: Rename a file or directory.

members.name: resolve
members.description: Resolves the given path string against this path.

members.name: resolveSibling
members.description: Resolves the given path string against this path's parent path.

members.name: scheme
members.description: Gets the file URI scheme, e.g. `s3://some-bucket/foo.txt` -> `s3`.

members.name: setPermissions
members.description: Sets a file's permissions using the [numeric notation](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File_system_permissions#Numeric_notation), i.e. as three digits representing the **owner**, **group**, and **other** permissions.

members.name: setText
members.description: Writes text to a file. Equivalent to setting the `text` property.

members.name: simpleName
members.description: Gets the file name without any extension, e.g. `/some/path/file.tar.gz` -> `file`.

members.name: size
members.description: Gets the file size in bytes.

members.name: splitCsv
members.description: Splits a CSV file into a list of records. See the {ref}`operator-splitcsv` operator for available options.

members.name: splitFasta
members.description: Splits a [FASTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FASTA_format) file into a list of records. See the {ref}`operator-splitfasta` operator for available options.

members.name: splitFastq
members.description: Splits a [FASTQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FASTQ_format) file into a list of records. See the {ref}`operator-splitfastq` operator for available options.

members.name: splitJson
members.description: Splits a JSON file into a list of records. See the {ref}`operator-splitjson` operator for available options.

members.name: splitText
members.description: Splits a text file into a list of lines. See the {ref}`operator-splittext` operator for available options.

members.name: text
members.description: Returns the file content as a string.

members.name: toUriString
members.description: Gets the file path along with the protocol scheme.

members.name: write
members.description: Writes a string to a file, replacing any existing content.

types.name: shim.Set
types.description:
A set is an unordered collection that cannot contain duplicate elements.

[Read more](https://nextflow.io/docs/latest/reference/stdlib.html#sete)

members.name: intersect
members.description: Returns the intersection of the set and the given iterable.

types.name: shim.String
types.description:
A string is an immutable sequence of characters.

[Read more](https://nextflow.io/docs/latest/reference/stdlib.html#string)

members.name: contains
members.description: Returns `true` if the string contains the given substring.

members.name: endsWith
members.description: Returns `true` if the string ends with the given suffix.

members.name: execute
members.description: Execute the string as a command. Returns a [Process](https://docs.groovy-lang.org/latest/html/groovy-jdk/java/lang/Process.html) which provides the exit status and standard input/output/error of the executed command.

members.name: indexOf
members.description: Returns the index within the string of the first occurrence of the given substring. Returns -1 if the string does not contain the substring.

members.name: isBlank
members.description: Returns `true` if the string is empty or contains only whitespace characters.

members.name: isDouble
members.description: Returns `true` if the string can be parsed as a 64-bit floating-point number.

members.name: isEmpty
members.description: Returns `true` if the string is empty (i.e. `length()` is 0).

members.name: isFloat
members.description: Returns `true` if the string can be parsed as a 32-bit floating-point number.

members.name: isInteger
members.description: Returns `true` if the string can be parsed as a 32-bit integer.

members.name: isLong
members.description: Returns `true` if the string can be parsed as a 64-bit integer.

members.name: lastIndexOf
members.description: Returns the index within the string of the last occurrence of the given substring, searching backwards starting at the given index. Returns -1 if the string does not contain the substring.

members.name: length
members.description: Returns the length of the string.

members.name: md5
members.description: Returns the MD5 checksum of the string.

members.name: readLines
members.description: Returns the lines of the string as a list.

members.name: replace
members.description: Returns a new string in which each occurrence of the target string is replaced with the given replacement string.

members.name: replaceAll
members.description: Returns a new string in which each occurrence of the given regular expression is replaced with the given replacement string.

members.name: replaceFirst
members.description: Returns a new string in which the first occurrence of the given regular expression is replaced with the given replacement string.

members.name: reverse
members.description: Returns a new string with the characters in reverse order.

members.name: sha256
members.description: Returns the SHA-256 checksum of the string.

members.name: startsWith
members.description: Returns `true` if the string starts with the given prefix.

members.name: strip
members.description: Returns a copy of the string with all leading and trailing whitespace removed.

members.name: stripIndent
members.description: Returns a copy of the string with leading spaces on each line removed. The number of spaces to remove is determined by the line with the least number of leading spaces, excluding lines with only whitespace.

members.name: stripLeading
members.description: Returns a copy of the string with all leading whitespace removed.

members.name: stripTrailing
members.description: Returns a copy of the string with all trailing whitespace removed.

members.name: substring
members.description: Returns a substring of this string.

members.name: toBoolean
members.description: Returns `true` if the trimmed string is "true", "y", or "1" (ignoring case).

members.name: toDouble
members.description: Parses the string into a 64-bit floating-point number.

members.name: toFloat
members.description: Parses the string into a 32-bit floating-point number.

members.name: toInteger
members.description: Parses the string into a 32-bit integer.

members.name: toLong
members.description: Parses the string into a 64-bit integer.

members.name: toLowerCase
members.description: Returns a copy of this string with all characters converted to lower case.

members.name: toUpperCase
members.description: Returns a copy of this string with all characters converted to upper case.

members.name: tokenize
members.description: Splits the string into a list of substrings using the given delimiters. Each character in the delimiter string is treated as a separate delimiter.

members.name: trim
members.description: Returns a copy of this string with leading and trailing whitespace removed.

featureFlags.name: nextflow.enable.configProcessNamesValidation
featureFlags.description: When `true`, prints a warning for every `withName:` process selector that doesn't match a process in the pipeline (default: `true`).

featureFlags.name: nextflow.enable.moduleBinaries
featureFlags.description: When `true`, enables the use of module-scoped executable scripts via [module resources](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/modules/developing-modules#resources).

featureFlags.name: nextflow.enable.strict
featureFlags.description: When `true`, the pipeline is executed in [strict mode](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/reference/feature-flags).

featureFlags.name: nextflow.enable.types
featureFlags.description:
When `true`, enables the use of [typed processes](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/process-typed) and [typed workflows](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/workflow-typed).

This feature flag must be enabled in every script that uses typed processes/workflows. Legacy processes/workflows can not be defined in scripts that enable this feature flag.

featureFlags.name: nextflow.preview.recursion
featureFlags.description: When `true`, enables the use of [process and workflow recursion](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/workflow#process-and-workflow-recursion).
